questions.question: Use filter_subcategories with subcategories_to_remove equal to Medium, High to characterize the sales differences among various brands when only the Low income customers are observed in order to know what are the sales differences among various brands for Low income customers?

answer.value: All five brands (ASICS, Puma, Reebok, New Balance, Adidas, Nike) show remarkably consistent performance across High, Medium, and Low income customer segments with minimal variation. ASICS leads with highest total average sales at 2.56 units, followed closely by Puma (2.53) and Reebok (2.49). The most striking observation is that income level has virtually no impact on sales performance across all brands, with all three income levels showing nearly identical average sales around 2.49-2.50 units. This suggests that brand preference and product characteristics drive purchase decisions more than customer income level in this footwear market

key_insights: All brands show minimal variation across income levels
Income level has virtually no impact on sales performance
ASICS leads with highest average sales at 2.56 units
Brand preference drives purchases more than customer income level
